recipes.name: Sweet and Savory Slow Cooker Pulled Pork

steps.text: Place the pork shoulder roast into a large plastic bag, pour 1 cup of root beer over the meat, and squeeze out all the air from the bag. Seal the bag closed, and refrigerate 6 hours to overnight.
The next day, mix together the light brown sugar, kosher salt, black pepper, paprika, dry mustard, onion powder, garlic salt, celery salt, cinnamon, ginger, and nutmeg in a bowl.
Remove the meat from the marinade, and shake off the excess. Rub the meat all over with the spice mixture, wrap in plastic wrap, and refrigerate for 30 minutes to 2 hours.
Mix together the balsamic vinegar, 1 1/2 cups of root beer, whiskey, and brown sugar in a bowl, and stir until the sugar dissolves.

Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat, and sear the meat on all sides until the meat develops a brown crust, about 3 minutes per side. Place the seared meat into a slow cooker. Pour the balsamic vinegar-root beer mixture over the meat, set the slow cooker to High, and cook for 6 to 8 hours.

Remove the roast from the slow cooker, and shred with 2 forks. Discard the bones and all but 1 cup of the liquid in the slow cooker. Return the shredded meat to the cooker, mix in the barbecue sauce, and let sit on Low until ready to serve. Serve piled on buns.

raw_recipe.headline: Sweet and Savory Slow Cooker Pulled Pork
raw_recipe.description: Low and slow defines this recipe for shredded pork, marinated overnight in root beer, rubbed with warm and flavorful spices, then slowly simmered for 6 hours in a slow cooker in a cooking sauce with more root beer, balsamic vinegar, and a shot of whiskey. The meat is shredded and served on soft buns.

video.description: For juicy, mouthwatering pulled pork, look no further than this simple and spectacular preparation for pulled pork. Marinate a pork shoulder roast in root beer overnight, then cover in a spicy rub of brown sugar, kosher salt, black pepper, paprika, dry mustard, onion powder, garlic salt, celery salt, cinnamon, ginger and nutmeg. Allow the roast to rest, then sear on all sides to develop a crust. Place in a slow cooker and cover with a sauce of balsamic vinegar, root beer, whiskey and brown sugar. Shred and mix with a little barbecue sauce and enjoy some incredibly tender and delicious pork!

review.reviewBody: If you are not following the steps I really don’t think it is fair for you to rate the recipe. All reviews are helpful, but rating a recipe poorly after you clearly state that you didn’t follow the steps seems a little unfair.

I think stayredbolt needs to chill out. If someone changes the recipe and then rates it, they are rating the changed recipe. I didn't do any of the marinating, didn't have rootbeer, cut the brown sugar in half, used an organic bbq sauce, used diced onions instead of onion powder, and used bourbon for whiskey, It came out great!!! I did braise the sides of the roast for 3 minutes each to add a crispy texture and lock in flavors. After cooking initially with fat on I then pulled the fat off for a cleaner end product. The pulled pork had great flavor and texture. I did follow the cooking instructions.

I thank stayredbolt for getting me started on the recipe but she needs to watch the Picasso series on PBS.

Made it tonight for dinner. I marinated it in A&W overnight (actually closer to 10 hours). Made the rub-did not have the mustard, celery salt, or onion powder so I added garlic powder-had everything else-left the rub on for an hour. I did not sear it as I was running short on time-I have problems with timing when cooking. Put the 4 pound pork tenderloin in the crock pot for 6 hours on high. I did mix the bbq sauce with 1 3/4 cups of liquid (rather than the called for 1 cup) as I like a moist bbq and was worried that b/c I had the tenderloin (which is more lean than the boston butt) that it might dry out when I stored it in the frig. It was almost too moist-so next time I will sear the meat and use less liquid (but I'll keep the extra just in case)! Great flavor-I'll be eating this for days.....unless my co-workers are lucky and I take some in tomorrow!

I have made this several times for a staff picnic (30+ people). The first time I followed the recipe exactly; after that I omitted the first step of marinating the pork overnight in root beer, and I really can't tell the difference. Other than that, I follow all the steps (although I quadruple the ingredients since I make about 14 pounds). I like it without that last step of adding BBQ sauce; the rub adds lots of flavor.

I've made this many times and it's always a hit. The spice rub is wonderful and adds great flavor (it doesn't just taste like bbq sauce ). Like others, I do not sear or marinate the meat. I do leave the pork shoulder overnight in the refrigerator with the dry rub on. I cook the pork on low for 8 hours. It's an easy, delicious crowd pleaser.

So although I did not marinate this over night and skipped the browning step ( I am pretty lazy but really liked the concept of this pulled pork) this turned out fantastic. One of my favorite recipes. The only changes I made ingredient wise was used Dr. Pepper instead of Root beer because of preference but I doubled the recipe (had a 10lb roast) and I cooked it on low for about 15 hours. It was incredible I imagine it would be just as amazing if you followed this too a T but even with my changes It was so good.

This is so good you don't even need bar bq sauce , My son and daughter in law love this. My son is allergic to bar bq sauce and my daughter in law doesn't like pork but this was a hit with both of them. It is the best recipe for this wonderful treat. I let mine set in the root beer for a couple of days in the fridge and than I put the spices in and let it set for at least a day in the fridge I then slow cook it and it is so tender and moist. If you like pulled pork try this recipe it's delicious .

Oh my goodness this was AMAZING. I had 10lbs of boneless pork, and I had to expedite it a bit due to time constraints. So I marinaded it in the root beer for about 2 hours, then in the rub for about a half hour. Also, not sure if it was because it was boneless, but I put it in the crock on LOW overnight, and in the morning it was falling apart! Absolutely to die for. Everyone was raving about it for days. DEFINITELY a keeper! Thank you!!

I have made this recipe twice, the first time I followed the recipe exact, the sauce was to thin making the bun soggy and the meat a bit bland. We didn't care for it. The second time I added a tablespoon of cornstarch to the reserved liquid and it thickened it up and we loved it. Only thing it needed in my opinion

Five stars isn't good enough for this recipe! I made it according to directions except it marinated in the spices overnight rather than two hours and used less barbecue sauce than called for. It was so good I hated to put barbecue sauce in it. Made it for a block party. The crock pot was empty at the end and 3 people went out of their way to tell me how good it was! I was going to let it cook for 8 hours but I tried it at the end of 6 hours and it was already falling off the bone. Make this, you can't go wrong.

Oh my gosh! This was fantastic! The only change I made was to skip all the prep work in the beginning. Added the rootbear, all the seasonings and spices (minus whiskey- none of us drink it), dropped in the meat and let it go for 6 hours. It was the best pulled pork I've ever had. My mom was begging for the recipe. If I could rate it 6/5 I would!
I made this last Christmas for my large family. Everyone loved it so much I’m making it again this Christmas. I make enough for leftovers because I love this recipe.
I make this every 4th of July and it’s a big hit! I serve it with homemade coleslaw, pickles and Hawaiian rolls Yum!!

I’ve made this dozens and dozens of times over the last decade and everyone who eats it with us raves about the flavor. Taking shortcuts still yields a good meal; but following all the steps produces the best flavor. I do it without the whiskey.

I followed the recipe pretty close., but I didn't sear the roast before slow cooking. I turned out really good anyway. I also cooked it on high for just one hour, then on low for about 8 more hours. It was tender and moist. Next time I probably won't add the cinnamon as I didn't care for the taste of it in the meat.
Very good the first night but when reheated leftovers the rootbeer flavor came out a bit too strong

This is actually the only pulled pork recipe that I truly love. The flavor is amazing! I know it may seem like a daunting amount of steps, but in the end, it’s just soaking the pork, dry rubbing it and then putting it in the slow cooker. In my opinion, this is the best recipe and I’m going to continue to use it as my only recipe for pulled pork.

There really isn't a LOT of steps to this recipe. I don't know why people are complaining. If you want to cook it correctly sometimes you need to do an extra step or two. Its well worth it. Kosher salt is used because table salt has chemicals added to it & kosher does not. It has nothing to do with religious practices.
